newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket-NSW stumble in Shield match against Queensland.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-NSW stumble in Shield match against Queensland.

text.p: Steve Waugh scored an unbeaten half century to steer New South Wales out of trouble on the first day of their Sheffield Shield match against Queensland at Bankstown Oval on Friday.
New South Wales lost three wickets in the second session to be 167 for four at tea, with Waugh on 67 and captain Greg Matthews 11 not out.

Australia captain Mark Taylor was the first New South Wales wicket to fall in the second session, caught by Mike Kasprowicz from the bowling of left-arm spinner Paul Jackson for 53 with the score on 105 for two.
Mark Waugh joined twin brother Steve at the crease on their suburban home ground but was caught behind by test wicketkeeper Ian Healy from the bowling of Kasprowicz for four.
All-rounder Shane Lee then fell cheaply to Kapsrowicz before Steve Waugh steadied his side's innings.
In Melbourne, former Australia player Dean Jones came to Victoria's rescue after the home side had collapsed to be 71 for four shortly after lunch in the match against South Australia.
By tea Jones and Harvey had reclaimed the initiative for Victoria to be 181 for four, with Jones on 80 and Harvey 59.
Opener Brad Hodge fell for 25 early in the second session before Laurie Harper fell nine balls later when he was caught by Adam Kimber from the bowling of spinner Peter McIntyre for four.
In Perth, Tasmania openers Dene Hills and Jamie Cox steered their side to 57 without loss at lunch on the first day of their match against Western Australia.
About 40 minutes of play had been lost in the first session due to rain.
